tasks.task: Build a logic model and theory of change

items.when: When a new programme or funding year starts and the whole evaluation year needs planning
When a programme needs one page from long-term change back to activities and inputs
When you want a second draft of the activity-to-outcome map with its evidence gaps listed
When a link in the chain looks too easy, to trace what each step really causes next
Before the model is agreed, to imagine the programme failed and name the weak assumptions

tasks.task: Scope the evaluation and set its questions

items.when: At the start of any evaluation, before measures or surveys are written
When the funder's question is broad, to split it into sub-questions and sources
When you must choose between surveys, interviews and records for each question
When a comparison group or a waiting list is possible and needs a fair design
When budget is small, to compare a light and a fuller evaluation with cost and dates

tasks.task: Choose outcome measures and write the data collection plan

items.when: When the logic model is agreed and the team needs a few measures they can really collect
When you have goals and existing records and need tracking dates, owners and report rules
When the measures are all end results, to add the inputs the team controls week to week
When a measure needs one agreed definition so two sites count it the same way

tasks.task: Write matched before-and-after surveys

items.when: When each outcome needs plain questions with the same wording, order and scale each time
Before writing, to see how many matched pairs you need to detect the change you hope for
When a staff or partner questionnaire is needed beside the participant survey
When the draft exists, to get a bias review, a shorter list and a pretest plan
When participants are young or read little English, to simplify each question

tasks.task: Write the survey consent and privacy page

items.when: Before any programme survey, interview or focus group goes out
When you start collecting something new, to see if it needs a full privacy review
When the data covers children or health, to write the assessment with conditions and owners

tasks.task: Run a survey round and check what came back

items.when: At each collection point in the plan: before, after and any follow-up
When staff need the participant code and the rules for pairing answers explained
When the returns arrive, to see missing values, odd entries and unusable columns
When answers were typed by hand and dates, numbers and spacing are inconsistent

tasks.task: Clean and match attendance and survey records

items.when: When records have duplicates, blanks and wrong types that would skew the counts
When the workbook has formulas, to reconcile totals and keep the formatting intact
When the same messy export arrives each term and the cleaning rules should be saved

tasks.task: Analyse matched survey and outcome data

items.when: When you have attendance, matched answers and outcome records to read outcome by outcome
When you need tables and charts from the export by asking in plain words
When you need the right test for a before and after change, explained plainly
When results must become a checked findings table with honest caveats on who answered
Before a result is reported, to score how far each question's answers can be trusted
When the group is small, for an honest read of what the numbers can support
When a change of a few points is about to be called an impact

tasks.task: State what the data can and cannot show

items.when: Before any report, funder update or board paper goes out
When a change is found, to list the rival explanations besides the programme
When a draft claims the programme caused a change, to grade the evidence behind it
When everyone wants the result to be true and nobody has tried to explain it another way

tasks.task: Write the evaluation report, outcome by outcome

items.when: When the analysis is done and each outcome needs its numbers, limits and what was learned
When the report closes the year and must feed next year's plan
When an outcome needs one clean chart drawn from the programme's own data
When charts are drafted, to check the chart type and axes do not overstate the change
When the findings read like a statistics paper and trustees must understand them
Before sign-off, to tie every figure in the report to the data file it came from
When a headline number needs its comparison and what it actually counts spelled out

tasks.task: Write a funder impact summary

items.when: When the full report exists and a funder needs two honest pages
When the funder reads one page, to put the answer first with the numbers behind it
When the funder wants a visual one-pager, to try the summary as an infographic
When the summary quotes averages and hides how results were spread across people
Before sending, to read it as the funder and list every claim they would question

tasks.task: Map outcomes to each funder's headings

items.when: When several funders ask for different outcome headings and reports
When two funders define the same measure differently, to reconcile with worked examples
When the map feeds a new bid and the evaluation section must match the funder's rules

tasks.task: Write a participant story from case notes

items.when: When a report needs one or two real stories that show how change happened
When several cases could be told, to pick the one to build on and its surprise
When the story names a person, to write it with consent and a way to withdraw
Before it is published, to check each detail of the story against the case notes

tasks.task: Build the monthly monitoring report and dashboard

items.when: When you have dated session records and need monthly counts and rates you can trace
When the same report must be rerun each month from the same sources
When staff and the board need two views of the measures, with owners and action points

tasks.task: Write metric definitions and a data dictionary

items.when: When the dictionary must list each measure's source, collector and timing
When each measure needs one written definition the whole team reuses
When a measure rests on a word like engaged or completed, to test it on hard cases

tasks.task: Gather and read interview evidence from participants

items.when: When numbers cannot explain why change happened and you need a small interview plan
When interviews are done, to rank themes by how often they come up, with quotes
Before any participant is interviewed or recorded

tasks.task: Review outside evidence that a programme model works

items.when: When a funder asks what the research says, to review sources chosen by clear rules
When every claim in the review must carry a source or be marked unsourced
When a school wellbeing programme needs the evidence linking it to academic results
When one study carries the case, to grade its design, bias and statistics

tasks.task: Write a board paper on what to keep, change or stop

items.when: When the year is over and the team needs one page on what to repeat and what to change
When trustees must make a decision and need results, risks and next steps
When results are good and the board asks if the programme is ready to grow
Before the paper goes to trustees, to state plainly what the evidence does not cover

tasks.task: Plan a needs assessment or baseline

items.when: When a new service needs a research plan, a map of other providers and gaps to check
When a teacher wants to collect evidence on one question in their own classroom
When the baseline must answer the same questions the final evaluation will ask

tasks.task: Check whether a course changed what people do

items.when: When a course has ended, to compare real work afterwards with the skills taught
When learners should be asked the same questions before the course and after it

tasks.task: Check the numbers in an annual or impact report

items.when: When the yearly report is planned and facts, numbers and names need checking before print
When the draft is laid out, to give every number a dated source or cut it
When the report's headline claims more than the data can support

always.when: Before any report or summary leaves, to tie each figure and quote to a dated source
Before a survey or report is shared, to catch typos and one outcome named two ways

helpers.when: When the findings must become a grant application or a report in a funder's own form
When the data needs joining across systems or statistics beyond a before and after read
When the evaluation needs focus groups or a full interview round with participants
When the report or dashboard needs designed charts, not one quick chart
When data on children, health or vulnerable adults raises privacy or safeguarding duties

gaps: The library is thin for this role: about 50 good fits, most of them general research and data items
Only one library item builds a logic model, and none offers two or three theory of change shapes to compare
No library item writes matched before-and-after surveys with participant codes or picks validated scales
No library item analyses paired before-and-after answers or reports effect sizes for small groups
No library item writes a consent and privacy page for surveys of children or vulnerable adults
No library item maps one set of outcomes to several funders' headings and report dates
No library item estimates cost per outcome or social return on investment
No library item designs an attendance and outputs tracker for sessions and participants
No library item removes names and identifying details from case notes before a story is written
No library item plans a focus group with programme participants or young people
No library item writes the monitoring and evaluation section of a grant proposal
No mind in the library is built on an evaluation thinker such as Michael Quinn Patton or Carol Weiss
